newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Imperial Tobacco BBB plus corp credit.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Imperial Tobacco BBB plus corp credit.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it had assigned its BBB plus corporate credit rating to Imperial Tobacco Group Plc.
"The rating reflects the general creditworthiness of Imperial Tobacco and is not currently assigned to any specific debt instrument," S&P said in a statement.

"The rating on Imperial Tobacco, with 1995 sales of 3.6 billion sterling and operating profit of 348 million sterling, reflects its pending status as an independent company following its expected de-merger from Hanson Plc on October 1, 1996," S&P said.

It said the key rating factors were Imperial Tobacco's number two position in the UK's highly consolidated cigarette market, combined with the very strong, stable cash generating characteristics of this business.
S&P said the outlook on the rating was stable.

"The likelihood of stepped-up competitive pressures from the international cigarette producers in its core UK market is mitigated by the well-entrenched position of the top two UK companies, who control over three-quarters of the UK market, and by UK consumers' preference for Virginia tobaccos sold by Imperial Tobacco and its UK peers, the angecy said.
It said the future growth prospects for the firm were modest, reflecting its more limited presence to date and funds to expand in international growth markets.
"As a result, it will remain challenged by declining UK consumption trends," S&P said.
"Nonetheless, the stable outlook is supported by the group's track record of consistent and strong cash flow generation," it added.
